summary: Backend-only verification of Field/Office Property parity iteration. Ran the two existing hermetic pytests (test_property_parity.py, test_mobile_property_patch.py) — both PASS. Added a new live HTTP test suite (test_field_property_live.py) against REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL exercising real auth + endpoints: 15/16 tests pass. All core guarantees confirmed live: (a) PATCH /api/mobile/properties/{id} toggles DNK on/off and updates notes for authorized caller; (b) Sales IDOR — unauthorized sales user is 403 on both GET and PATCH of /api/mobile/properties/{id}; (c) all six canonical outcomes (no_answer, not_interested, interested, callback, appointment, do_not_knock) accepted on POST /api/mobile/visits; (d) invalid outcomes (sold, maybe) rejected with 422 on BOTH mobile and office visit endpoints; (e) office accepts callback+appointment; (f) visit notes persist and appear in property visits[]; (g) GET /api/mobile/properties/{id} exposes all canonical keys PLUS compat aliases owner_name/owner_phone/existing_lead_id and they equal canonical owner contact / lead_id. One minor wire-level parity mismatch found (see below).

minor.issue: Wire-format datetime parity: Office response serializes visit timestamps via Pydantic ('2026-08-29T21:08:26.802164Z') while Mobile response serializes via raw dict isoformat ('2026-08-29T21:08:26.802164+00:00'). Semantic values are identical (same instant), but the strings differ, so a JSON-level byte comparison of visits[]/created_at/updated_at is NOT byte-parity. Consumers doing string equality (or naive parsing) may treat them as different. Suggest routing the mobile response through the same Pydantic model / a single datetime serializer so office and field emit byte-identical timestamp strings. Hermetic in-process test doesn't catch this because both paths yield equal Python datetime objects — only serialized JSON diverges.

action_items: Unify datetime serialization between office and mobile Property detail responses so visit timestamps are byte-identical strings (route mobile through Pydantic model or apply the same isoformat/Z formatter used by Office).
critical_code_review_comments: services/property_detail.build_property_detail returns Python datetime objects and Office wraps them in a Pydantic model (yielding 'Z'-suffixed ISO strings), while routers.mobile.get_property returns the dict directly — FastAPI's json encoder falls back to datetime.isoformat() (yielding '+00:00'). This breaks pure wire-parity on created_at/updated_at/visits[].visited_at/visits[].created_at. Consider defining a single PropertyDetail pydantic model shared by both routers.

rca of the issue: Datetime-parity minor issue: mobile router returns a raw dict; FastAPI's default jsonable_encoder serializes datetime via .isoformat() -> '+00:00'. Office router returns a Pydantic model that produces '...Z' via its json_encoder config. Fix: share a PropertyDetail Pydantic model between routers, or apply a common datetime json_encoder in mobile as well.
